objective: Describe the implications and internal coherence of the current organization-level all-event IRIS priors without fitting, validating, changing, or recommending them.

frozen_model.magnitude_transformation: fit Lognormal(mu,sigma) with the configured median and p95

aggregate_outputs: analytic expected event count and zero-event/at-least-one-event probabilities
simulated zero-loss fraction and annual-loss mean, median, p75, p90, p95, and p99
conditional-positive annual-loss mean, median, p90, p95, and p99
probability of exceeding each frozen dollar point
share of total simulated loss in the top one percent of organization-years
minimum and maximum batch mean and p95 as Monte Carlo stability diagnostics

coherence_checks: The transformed Poisson rate reproduces the configured annual probability of at least one event to absolute tolerance 1e-12.
The fitted lognormal reproduces the configured magnitude median and p95 to relative tolerance 1e-12.
The simulated zero-loss fraction is within 0.005 absolute of the analytic zero-event probability.
The annual-loss median is zero because the analytic zero-event probability exceeds one half.
Every reported exceedance probability is between zero and one and is nonincreasing as the frozen dollar point rises.
Repeating the fixed seed and inputs produces byte-identical aggregate JSON.
The production store remains byte-identical and no SimulationRun, RiskScenario, or PriorSource row is written.

permitted: Describe internal source reproduction, skew, zero mass, tail concentration, fixed-point exceedance, and Monte Carlo batch variability.
State that these are implications of the configured industry baseline for an anonymous neutral organization-year.
Identify population applicability and epistemic uncertainty as unresolved limitations.
prohibited: Claim calibration, predictive validity, accuracy, representativeness, decision quality, remediation value, or portfolio optimality.
Compare against observed outcomes, select a preferred model, fit parameters, infer cohorts, or recommend a threshold.
Treat Monte Carlo variability as epistemic prior uncertainty or confidence in real-world performance.
Use the results for deal, budget, risk-acceptance, remediation, or production-policy decisions.

decision_rule: Passing coherence checks establishes only that the frozen implementation reproduces and consistently simulates the configured prior implications. It does not clear the OPT-014 data gate. The result must retain the choice between governed independent-data acquisition and bounded negative-feasibility closure.
excluded: Network access, uploads, provider calls, tokens, or cost
Production-store reads beyond before/after hashing or any store mutation
Repository, finding, assessment, label, source, incident, loss, or organization identity access
Raw simulated draw persistence or persisted SimulationRun/RiskScenario/PriorSource rows
Observed-outcome validation, fitting, model comparison, backtesting, resampling, or adequacy thresholds
New or changed priors, hierarchical estimation, category allocation, remediation effects, dependencies, or portfolio optimization
Tuning, recalibration, threshold selection or recommendation, production-policy changes
OPT-014 promotion or closure, OPT-010 execution, branch integration, remote push, or deployment
